title: Reactive astrocytes
objective: Explain how astrocytes become reactive and that reactivity can be harmful or helpful.

steps.title: The other glia
steps.body: **[[astrocyte|Astrocytes]]** support neurons, manage ions and transmitters, and help form the [[blood–brain barrier]]. In injury they become **[[reactive astrocyte|reactive]]** (upregulating markers like GFAP). Some reactive astrocytes, induced by activated microglia, are neurotoxic; others are protective.

flag.note: The neurotoxic-vs-protective split (the old A1/A2 labels) is debated; the field now describes astrocyte states more carefully.

steps.prompt: What can trigger astrocytes to become reactive and even neurotoxic?
options: Loss of GFAP expression by the astrocyte itself
Direct physical damage to the astrocyte, and nothing else
A drop in neuronal firing in the surrounding tissue
steps.explanation: Activated microglia can induce a neurotoxic reactive-astrocyte state — a glia-to-glia signal that couples the two in neuroinflammation.

variants.setup: Microglia are strongly activated in a region.
variants.prompt: What can happen to nearby astrocytes?
options: They can be induced into a reactive, sometimes neurotoxic state
They lose GFAP and stop supporting the neurons
They are unaffected; microglial signals act only on neurons
variants.reveal: Activated microglia can drive astrocytes into a reactive, potentially neurotoxic state.

steps.setup: A slide is captioned 'reactive astrocytes' but shows the normal, sparse GFAP pattern.
options: The sparse baseline pattern isn't the reactive, upregulated one
GFAP is downregulated when astrocytes become reactive
Reactive astrocytes lose their processes and look smaller
GFAP labels only the astrocyte endfeet on blood vessels
steps.reveal: Reactive astrocytes upregulate GFAP and change shape; a sparse baseline pattern is the resting reference, not reactivity. GFAP alone doesn't define a reactive state, but it's the usual first marker. (This was a real fix in our B5 microscope slide.)

options: Upregulated GFAP, not the sparse baseline pattern
GFAP being downregulated as astrocytes react
Astrocytes shrinking and losing their processes
variants.explanation: Reactivity means upregulated GFAP and altered morphology, unlike the sparse baseline.

sources.note: Reactive astrocytes induced by activated microglia can be neurotoxic.
